notes.decision: 'Deceits' — Lyc. ⲭⲗⲟⲡⲉ = Sah. ϭⲗⲟⲡⲉ 'deceit, secret thing'. Plural here designates the three cosmic deceits (water/darkness/fire) hidden in the bodies of the archons. Continues from previous page.
'Stricken/afflicted' — qualitative or relative form, root unclear. Possibly from ϩⲱⲱⲥ/ϩⲱϣ 'afflict' or related to ⲥⲱⲡ/ⲥⲱⲡⲥⲡ 'wounded.' Context (man with disease) is unambiguous.
Greek loanword πληγή 'blow, wound, plague' — the dotted variants are scribal. Pairs with ⲓⲁⲃⲉ/ϣⲱⲛⲉ as the bodily afflictions the physician treats.
'Other poisons' — ⲙⲏⲧⲉ 'poison, venom' (Crum 192b) with ⲕⲉ- prefix and -ⲟⲩ plural. Pairs with χολή 'gall' as toxic humors in the diseased body.
Greek loanword εὐκαιρία 'good occasion, opportune moment' — the medical timing for treatment.

'(He) finds' — recurring verb opening each new medicine in the parable (lines 5, 6, 7). Lycopolitan verb form of uncertain root, possibly contracted from ϩⲏⲧ + ⲥⲱⲧⲡ̄ ('elect with mind') or ⲛⲏϫ 'apply.' Translated 'find' on contextual parallelism with the parable's three medicaments.
'Out against the taste' — antidote works against the bitter taste/savor of the disease. ⲧⲡⲧⲉ = ⲧⲡⲉ 'taste' (already in glossary).
'Purgative' — agent-noun ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who') + ϣⲟⲩⲟ ('pour out'). Standard agentive formation paralleling ⲣⲉϩ†ⲥⲃⲱ 'teacher.' Names a medicine that purges/evacuates the lower body's disease.
'To soothe' — ⲗⲁⲅⲉ likely from ⲗⲱⲕϩ̄ 'soft, sweet' or ⲗⲱⲕⲍ 'sweeten' — fits soothing medicine for blows/wounds. ⲛ̄- here functions as infinitive marker.
'The Living Spirit himself' — ⲍⲱϩ = Lyc. reflexive ϩⲱⲱϥ, intensifying the subject. Standard Manichaean cosmological figure (third member of the second emanation).
'The healing' — verbal noun from ⲧⲁⲗϭⲟ 'heal, cure.' The three garments are 'medicines of the healing' worn by the Living Spirit upon his cosmic body.

'That of the wind, that of the water, with that of the fire' — the three garments of the Living Spirit (cf. K.39 'three garments'). Note that ⲡⲙⲁⲩ here is 'water' (= ⲙⲟⲟⲩ); contrasts with the deceits-triplet (water/darkness/fire) where ⲙⲁⲩ also = water. The dark-water deceit is countered by the wind-garment, the dark-darkness deceit by the water-garment, the dark-fire deceit by the fire-garment.
'Single-mindedness' — already in glossary; the Living Spirit's unified manifestation in revealing himself to the upper archons.

'An expulsion forth' — ϣⲛϣ root unclear; possibly Lyc. ϣⲱⲛⲥ 'plunder, ravage' or ϣⲛ̄ϣ̄ 'service.' Context (revealing self forth, then pouring out the three deceits) suggests an expulsive/cleansing action. Tentative; flagging for parallels.

'The marrow' — literally ⲡⲁⲧ-ⲕⲉⲥ 'that-of-the-bone,' i.e. the substance within the bone. First (innermost) of the seven body-layers in the womb-child schema. Sequence: marrow → bone → sinew → flesh → vein → bond → skin.

'The bond' — sixth in the seven-part body series. Already in glossary as 'bond, fetter,' but here in anatomical register it likely names ligament/connective tissue (that-which-binds-together). Maintained as 'bond' for terminological consistency.
'The other garment' — ⲕⲉ- 'other' + ⲍⲃⲥ 'garment' (= ϩⲃⲥⲱ). The womb-child's body itself is one garment; the actual cloth garments after birth are the 'other garment.'
Translated 'the man' (= ⲡⲣⲱⲙⲉ); the spelling ⲣ̄ⲱⲙⲛ with final -ⲛ is irregular but the morphology of the relative ⲉⲧⲟ́ⲁⲗⲉ ⲁⲣⲁⲥ ('who is mounted upon her') confirms a personal-noun reading.

Rendered 'the giving of the Youth' on the analysis ⲡ-ⲧⲁ-ϯ-ⲥ as a relative perfect or nominalized ϯ 'give.' Other readings (ⲡⲧⲁⲡ-ϯⲥ 'head/portion-given') possible. Context (the Youth = Third Power) leaves the precise referent unclear.

Translated 'eight teachings.' ⲙⲛⲧⲭⲙⲏⲛ = ⲙⲛⲧϣⲙⲏⲛ (with regular Lyc ⲭ for ϣ) = 'eight,' parallel to ⲙⲛⲧⲝⲙⲏⲛ in glossary. The kephalaion presumably enumerates three teachings + five further items totalling eight.

Rendered 'the bond of the offspring.' ⲡϣⲛⲁϣ tentatively read as a Lyc form related to ⲥⲛⲁϩ/ⲥⲛⲁⲍ 'bond, fetter' (already in glossary); ⲧⲙⲏⲥⲉ = ⲙⲓⲥⲉ 'offspring, that which is born/begotten.' Alternative readings 'swarm/multitude' possible. Confidence moderate.
Rendered 'a wound and a blow.' ⲡⲱⲍ = ⲡⲱϩ 'wound, breach'; ⲍⲓ = ϩⲓ 'and'; ⲡⲗⲏⲅⲏ = πληγή 'blow, stroke.' Standard Manichaean wound-doublet for cosmic injury.

Translated 'the strongholds.' ⲙⲁⲛⲝⲗⲟⲣⲉ = ⲙⲁⲛϫⲱⲣⲉ 'place-of-strong = stronghold/fortress' (glossary). Recurs throughout this page as the cosmic prison-encirclements that bind the dark teachings (Mother, Darkness, Fire).
Tentatively read as relative + ⲟⲩⲉⲛ 'open' (qualitative of ⲟⲩⲱⲛ): 'which are open(ed).' Could alternatively be ⲉⲧⲟⲩ-ⲟⲩⲉⲛ 'whom they open/manifest.' The fragmentary ⲁⲧ̣ϩ following may be a privative.

Translation deliberately left as placeholder/uncertain. Possible readings: (1) ⲧⲙⲉⲩ-ⲧⲟⲩ 'their mother' (with assimilation), fitting line 16's 'teaching of the Mother'; (2) ⲧⲙⲏⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩ 'their truth'; (3) ⲧⲙⲏⲧⲉ ⲛ̄ⲧⲟⲩ 'their midst.' Paired with [ⲡⲙ̄]ⲟⲩ 'the death' suggests a paired cosmic principle. Flagged for parallels.

Translated 'their hatred.' ⲙⲉⲍⲧ = Lyc ⲙⲉⲥⲧⲉ 'hatred' (per glossary entry ⲡⲉϩⲙⲉⲍⲧⲉ 'his hatred'). The image: archons whose veins (= conduits of life) and hatred (= affective principle) are both 'full beneath them' — the dark interior they carry.

Translated 'she drove down,' taking ⲥⲱⲍⲣⲉ as Lyc reflex of ⲥⲱϩⲣ̄/ⲥⲁϩⲣⲉ 'drive away, expel.' Already attested on prior page in glossary as ⲥⲱⲝⲧ/ⲥⲱⲣ-class. Pairs with ⲁϩⲍⲱⲕⲉ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'she drew forth' as the cosmogonic verb-pair for the Wind-teaching's act on the shadow of destruction.

Translated 'she bound (it/her).' Lyc ⲙⲁⲣⲥ̄ = ⲙⲟⲩⲣ + 3sg.f object 'bind her.' Stronghold-binding is the consummating act in each of the three teachings (Wind, Fire) — the dark substance is driven down, drawn forth, then bound in the encircling cosmic prison.

Translated 'the Wall of the Great Fire.' ⲥⲁⲃⲧ = ⲥⲟⲃⲧ̄ 'wall' (capitalized as named cosmic structure); ⲛⲁⲟ́ = ⲛⲁϭ 'great.' The outermost cosmic firewall in Manichaean cosmology, paralleling the wall of darkness around the cosmos in line 23.

Translated 'strip bare/naked.' Lyc ⲕⲁⲕ ⲁϩⲏⲩ 'strip naked' (= ⲕⲱⲕ ⲁϩⲏⲩ in glossary). Used metaphorically of the apostle's progressive unveiling of the three teachings — not all at once, but each at its appointed kairos.
Lit. 'he added unto his hand' — standard Coptic idiom for resumption of speech. Translated 'he continued' to convey natural English flow while preserving the additive sense.
Lyc. variant of ⲡⲉϫⲁϥ 'he said.' Subject understood as the Apostle/Illuminator from prior chapter context, not restored here as the line is intact.
ϣⲟⲩⲟ 'pour out, scatter, empty' with 3pl object suffix -ⲟⲩ. Translated 'scattered them out' — preserves the dispersive semantics that fits the cosmological context of evils being driven from heavens.

Read ⲡ̄ as defective ⲡⲉ (copula): 'it is a food and a profit.' ⲛⲁϩⲣⲉ = 'food/nourishment' (Crum); ⲍⲏⲩ = ϩⲏⲩ 'profit, gain.' The expelled dark substances become refining-material for the cosmic Twelve Great Works.

Reduplicated form of ϩⲱⲡ 'hide, conceal' with 3pl object suffix. The cosmic-architectural sealing of the dark powers outside the worlds in the climes/zones. 'Concealed/hid them' preserves the binding semantics.

ⲕⲁⲟ = ⲕⲉⲟⲩⲁ 'another (one)'; ⲛ̄ⲧⲍⲱⲛⲏ 'of the Zone.' Read 'to the other (region) of the Zone' — the cosmic geography where the dark dwelling-places are exiled, beyond the world-system into the surrounding cosmic Zone.

notes.coptic_form: ⲡϣⲁⲣⲡ ⲛⲍⲱⲃ ⲡⲉ ⲡⲉⲓ̈, ⲝⲉⲕⲁⲁⲥ ⲛⲉ
notes.decision: ⲛⲉ here functions as negative purpose marker (Lyc. for ⲛ̄ⲛⲉ-, negative future III after ϫⲉⲕⲁⲥ). The teleological structure: 'this is the first work, in order that [the evil] may not abound.'

Plural of ⲙⲟⲩⲓ̈ 'lion.' In Manichaean cosmology the lion is the head-form of the King of Darkness (cf. accumulated vocab ⲡⲙⲟⲩⲓ̈). 'The lions' here refers to the lion-archons that would have remained in the heavens had they not been driven down.

ⲧⲗ̄ⲧⲗ̄ 'drop, dripping' — the dripping/condensation of dark substance descending from above. Distinct from ⲧⲱⲗⲧⲗ 'be troubled.' The fire and the dripping form a parallel pair as the descending dark elements.
Greek ἐπιθυμία 'desire, concupiscence' — already attested in glossary entry ⲙⲛⲧⲟⲩⲁϩⲓⲏⲧ as Coptic equivalent. Standard Manichaean negative-cosmological term for the principle of carnal craving.
Read as a directional 'to the lower part' — possibly Lyc. variant of ⲁⲡⲉⲥⲏⲧ or related to ⲍⲏⲧ 'foot/foundation/below.' Distinct from but synonymous with ⲁⲡⲓⲧⲛⲉ used elsewhere on the page.
ⲟ́ⲱ = ϭⲱ 'remain, continue.' Periphrastic construction 'would-continue drawing' = 'would keep on drawing.' Preserves the durative aspect of the counterfactual.

ⲁϣⲁⲓ̈ 'be/become numerous, multiply' with imperfect ⲛⲉ-... ⲡⲉ. Translated 'they would have multiplied' — the apodosis of the counterfactual: had the expulsion not occurred, evil would have multiplied through trees, flesh, etc.
ⲧⲃⲁ = '10,000 / myriad'; ϣⲟ = '1000.' The ratio: 'the ten-thousand that exists in the thousand men' — i.e., ten thousand evils in every thousand men. Preserves the numerical hyperbole.

ⲡⲥⲁⲩⲛⲉ 'knowledge'; ⲛⲱⲥⲕ from ⲱⲥⲕ 'tarry, be long' (cf. ⲉⲥⲕⲉ in glossary). 'Long' here probably modifies the duration: 'the thought and the knowledge of [a long time]' — the cognitive faculties' duration would have been radically diminished without the cosmic separation.
ⲧⲱⲡ 'shut up, gather, enclose' with 3sg.f object. Continues the negative-conditional series of expulsion-acts; here the final containment in the river of fire that surrounds the cosmos.

'The river of fire that surrounds the worlds' — the cosmological river (cf. glossary ⲙⲁⲝⲓⲟⲣⲉ 'river') of fire encircling the world-system, into which the captive fire-substance is finally bound. ⲕⲱⲧⲉ here = 'surround, encircle' (distinguished from homophonous 'pluck' / 'building').

Initial ⲣⲉ taken as Lycopolitan reduction of circumstantial converter ⲉⲣⲉ-, governing the future ⲛⲁⲣ̄-ⲡⲍⲟⲩⲟ 'shall predominate.' This produces a temporal-circumstantial 'while...' clause introducing the chapter — the diagnostic condition (Fire of Darkness predominating) under which the body of the chapter is delivered.

Lexeme uncertain. Translated tentatively as 'the tree' on the basis of natural pairing with ⲡⲕⲁⲣⲡⲟⲥ 'the fruit.' Possibly a corrupt or scribal-variant spelling of ⲡϣⲏⲛ 'tree' or related to ⲧⲱϩⲛ 'mix' / ⲧⲱϩⲙ 'call.' Flagged for parallel attestations.

Lycopolitan negative existential construction. The form ⲕⲁⲟⲛ appears here to function as the existential element negated by ⲛⲉ-/ⲉⲛ; cf. parallel line 4 ⲛⲉⲕⲁⲟⲛ ⲟⲩⲣⲱⲙⲉ ⲛⲟⲩⲱⲧ 'there is not a single man' and line 22 ⲉⲕⲁⲟⲛ ⲛⲣⲡⲏⲩⲉ 'there is not (a one of) the temples.' Translated 'it was not (such)' / 'there is not.'

Translated as 'this single Evil' — taking ⲁ-ϯ- as demonstrative-article complex (Lyc. variant of ⲧⲉⲓ-) + κακία 'evil/vice.' The 'three types' suggests three modes/forms in which this single Evil manifested and was purified. Alternative reading as Greek ἀκακία 'innocence' is possible but less likely given the verb ⲧⲟⲩⲃⲁⲥ 'they purified it' which points to evil-as-object-of-purification.

ⲙⲁⲛⲟⲩⲱⲥ̄ parsed as ⲙⲁ-ⲛ̄-ⲟⲩⲱⲥ̄ 'place of harvest,' from ⲱⲉⲥ 'reap' (already in glossary). The Fourth Work concerns the apostles purifying their threshing-floor / place of reaping — fitting the agricultural-eschatological frame.

Plural of ⲣⲡⲉ 'temple,' here 'the temples (of the upper place).' Distinct from ⲣⲣⲟ 'king' / ⲣⲡⲟ 'kingship.' The temples are 'united' (ⲉⲩⲧⲏⲧ) and 'completed forth' (ⲉⲩⲭⲏⲕ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ) — the eschatological condition of the heavenly sanctuaries.

ⲫⲩⲥⲓ taken as Greek φύω 'grow, sprout, generate-by-nature' substantivized/verbalized — 'they shall sprout themselves.' The Seventh Work then concerns the souls' self-sprouting/regeneration at the cosmic rivers, leading to their arrival at their proper places and regions (line 25). Alternatively φύσει 'by nature.'

Reduplicated form likely from ⲭⲁⲗⲭ 'fashion together, mingle' (already in glossary), giving 'great fashionings' — i.e. final cosmological constructions/preparations paired with ⲥⲃⲧⲉⲩⲉ 'preparations.' Could alternatively be a joy-term (cf. ⲧⲉⲗⲏⲗ).
ⲧⲡ̄ taken as ⲧⲡⲉ 'head, beginning' — 'the head/beginning of the dissolution-forth of the world.' Marks the inception of cosmic dissolution as the contained item of the Ninth Work.
Form uncertain at line-end. Possibly ϩⲁⲣⲟⲕ 'before/unto you (sg.)' or 'alone, by yourself.' Translated tentatively 'to you'; flagged for review.

Translated 'depart' — Lyc ⲟⲩⲱⲗ 'go away, depart' parallels the preceding ⲟⲩⲓ̈ⲛⲉ 'pass' as a synonymous verb of removal. The pair ('does not pass forever, neither does it depart') describes the Land of Light's permanence.

Translated 'The twelfth: that you should also set down' — taking ⲧⲧⲙⲁⲍⲙⲛⲧⲥⲛⲁⲩⲥ as ordinal 'the twelfth' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲡⲙⲁⲍⲙⲛⲧⲥⲛⲁⲩⲥ); ⲉⲕⲁⲟⲛ as ⲉ-ⲕⲁ-ⲟⲛ 'that you place/set still' (2sg with ⲕⲱ + ⲟⲛ 'again, still'). The verbal sense is uncertain.
Translated 'the Half-region' per accumulated vocabulary; the Half designates the cosmic region whose works are hidden from the Aeons of Light.
Translated 'they were banished out' — ⲥⲁⲍⲣ = Lyc ⲥⲱϩⲣ̄ 'drive away, banish' + ⲁⲃⲁⲗ 'forth.' Captures the spatial expulsion of the Mighty Ones from the firmaments to the earth.

Translated 'yet not from the earth alone' — taking ⲭⲛ̄ as adversative 'but, yet' (parallel to ϫⲛ̄ in Sahidic). The structure contrasts banishment from the firmaments-to-earth with banishment from yet a higher region (the honor).
